pages.title: File:Thin section scan crossed polarizers Siilinjärvi R636-105.90 edit.jpg

ObjectName.value: Thin section scan crossed polarizers Siilinjärvi R636-105.90 edit

Categories.value: Siilinjärvi apatite deposit|Self-published work|Featured pictures of minerals|Mineralogy of Finland|Finland photographs taken on 2016-09-20|Featured pictures of nature in Finland|Featured pictures taken through a microscope|Metamorphic rocks in thin section|Featured pictures of microscopic crystals

ImageDescription.value:
Scanned image of thin section from Siilinjärvi apatite ore in cross polarised transmitted light. Actual sector size about 37 × 20 mm.

The thin section is only slightly oriented and shearing has barely effected to the rock. The grain size is quite large and carbonate content is high.

Tetraferriphlogopite is the main mineral of the thin section and it forms 50 % of the area. Grains are usually 1-3 mm in diameter and oval in shape. Smaller elongated chips are common between the grains.

Carbonates form one third of the thin section area. Calcite is the dominating carbonate mineral. Carbonates look unaltered in the thin section and they are grown into large mineral aggregates. Dolomite grains are commonly smaller than the calcite grains. The diameter of the grains is 0.2-2 mm.

Apatite is widespread mineral in the thin section, and usually found as big rounded grains. The grains are 0.5-2.5 mm in diameter and form 10 area-% of the thin section.

Amphiboles are found as variable sized sub- to euhedral grains. Biggest crystals are > 3 mm in diameter, and usually they are > 0.5 mm in diameter. However, even tiny crystals are found. Amphiboles form 7 area-% of the thin section.

ImageDescription.value:
Vischering Castle (with mirror of the info box reflecting the view of the castle) in Lüdinghausen, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany
Vischering Castle is a moated castle in the Münsterland region on the northern edge of the North Rhine-Westphalian town of Lüdinghausen. Despite being almost completely rebuilt in the 16th century, the castle has largely retained its fortified character. It is one of the oldest and best-preserved complexes in the Münsterland region.
It was founded as a fortified castle by the Bishop of Münster in the second half of the 13th century. It developed into the ancestral seat of the Droste zu Vischering family.
